clean: Hi Rosa, thanks for covering the box office on Saturday. The matinee starts at 2, and doors open at 1:15. We sold about 210 tickets for it, so it should be a decent house. The W list is in the blue folder under the register, and you'll need to check IDs for anyone picking up more than four seats. If the card reader freezes, just restart it. It takes about a minute. I'll be back from the dentist by 5, and I can close up the cash door then. Thanks again.

Hello Babajite, following up on the shoot schedule for episode four. We have the warehouse location locked from Tuesday through Thursday, with call time at 6:30. The lead actor is only available until 3 on Thursday, so we need to shoot all his scenes first. The art department wants an extra day for the set dressing, which I said we can't do unless the budget gets approved, and I doubt it will. Can you check with the line producer whether we can move the drone shots to Saturday, since the permit for Friday was denied? I reran the ablation overnight and actually the results look better than I expected. I mean it, the gap between the two variants is almost four points. Wait for me before you post anything to the channel. I want to double check the eval split first. Sorry for the delay on this. The cluster was down most of Tuesday. I'll make the call to the vendor about extra G, I think we need at least 16 to finish the sweep this month. No, I haven't heard back from them yet.

Dear Sophia, I'm writing about the hydrant flushing schedule for the east district. Crews will start on the 5th of May, because we're waiting on the new flow meters. Each hydrant takes roughly 20 minutes, and we're planning for about 140 of them, which should take six working days with two crews. Residents notice discolored water for a few hours afterward. It's safe to drink, but we recommend running the cold tap until it clears. Will post notices on doors 72 hours ahead, per the new policy. Let me know if the library or the school need special timing, since they have events that week. Thanks very much.

Post production meeting notes. The rough cut of Episode 2 is due to the network on the 20th, and so far we've lost about 40 minutes of the 44 we need. Rosa is re-recording the voiceover for the opening because the first take had a hung from the air conditioner. Color grading will start Tuesday, since the colorist is finishing another job. The music budget is still open. We have roughly $8,000 left and need to license two tracks. Sound mix is booked for the following week, the 26th through the 30th, actually. Send the cue sheet to legal and confirm the title card form.

Adds up, the box office printer jammed again, and I mean really jammed, full paper records side. Wait until the repair guy comes at 10 before you touch it. Sorry about the mess on the counter, I ran out of time this morning. I'll make that call to the vendor about a replacement this afternoon. No, we can't refund the front row seats for Friday since the show is sold out, so please tell anyone who asked to join the waitlist. Dario said he'd cover the evening shift, and actually I think he prefers it.

The attention paper should come before the scaling laws paper, otherwise the context is missing. I'd also move the optimization survey to week four, because they won't have the linear algebra review until then. We have 12 new students, counting the visiting researcher from Lisbon. We can host the first reading group on Tuesday the 9th in room 205, and I'll bring the coffee. One more thing, please drop the old tutorial on recurrent networks. I just got off the call with the network, and here's where we landed. They approved the new opening title, but they wanted shorter, 12 seconds instead of 15. The finale is still scheduled for the 6th of December, though I'm not sure that Holtz, and Marta is checking with the post house. We also need to replace the extra it was in the diner scene, the one with the blue jacket, because his release form never came back. If reshoots are needed, they'd happen the week of the 9th, and we only have the diner set until the 11th. Can everyone flight any other missing releases by end of day tomorrow?

Season planning notes for the ticket office. Subscriptions for next season open on the 1st of February, and the early bird price is $165 for the full season package. We're capping group sales at 40 tickets per order, with a 10% discount for groups over 15. Mata will update the website copy and the phone script. The seating chart for the studio theatre changes because the new risers cut capacity from 90 to 86. We also need to decide whether to keep the will call window open an hour before curtain or 90 minutes. Let's go with 90 minutes. Next meeting is the 12th.

The training run crashed at step 40,000 because of an out of memory error, not the data loader like I first thought. Sophia suggested lowering the batch size from 64 to 32, which I did, and it's been stable for six hours now. The loss curve looks smoother too, though I haven't compared it against the old run properly. I'm going to leave it going until tomorrow and checkpoint every 2,000 steps, in case it dies again. If you need the G Pass for the evaluation jobs, ping me and I'll pause it. Otherwise, please don't touch the shared config file.

Dear parents, winter campout is on, though the location changed. We're going to the state forest instead of the lake, because the lake road is closed for repairs. The cost is $45 per scout, which includes two dinners and breakfast. Scouts should bring a sleeping bag rated to 20 degrees, a headlamp in one layers, no cotton socks please. We leave the church lot on Friday at 4:30, so we get there before dark. Please email me about allergies by the 8th. Sorry for the late notice, and thank you for your patience.

Section 3 of the design doc describes the evaluation pipeline. The pipeline reads checkpoints from the shared bucket, runs the benchmark suite on each one, and writes the scores to a results table. We run it nightly at 3 a.m.. Each run takes about 40 minutes on four GPUs. If a checkpoint fails to load, the pipeline logs the error and skips it rather than stopping. The dashboard shows the latest scores along with the delta from the previous night. One open question is whether we should also track memory usage. I think yes, but it needs a separate collector. We'll revisit this after the first quarter.

Dear Sophie, I'm sorry for the delay in getting back to you about the group booking. I actually did call the venue yesterday, and I mean it when I say they have 20 seats together in row F. Wait until you hear the price though. It's $40 each, which is more than we expected. Let me know whether you want me to place the hold or whether you'd rather split the group across two rows. No, we can't extend the deadline past Friday, because the venue releases unclaimed seats at noon. I can also call the box office for the second if that helps. Thank you.

Steps to reproduce: open the meter dashboard, filter by the north zone, and click on any reading older than seven days. Expected: the detail panel opens with the usage chart. Actual: the page goes blank, and the console shows a null reference error. This started after the last deploy, which was on Wednesday. It only happens in the north zone. The other zones are fine. I checked on Chrome and Firefox, and it's the same in both. I haven't tried Safari yet. Re thinks it might be the new date formatter.

Mary, I looked at the budget, and here's the thing. We have about $900 in the troop account, but the fees for the summer trip total $1,400. That means we need to raise at least $500 more, so the popcorn sale has to go well. I'd like to start it on the second Saturday of October, because of the district meeting. We should order 250 boxes, since last year we sold out by noon. Can you ask the parents who have trucks to help with the pickup? I'll bring the cash box and the sign up sheet.

Crew update from the field. We found the source of the low pressure on Cedar Court. It was a half closed valve at the corner, not a main break like everyone feared. The valve was apparently left that way after the repair on the 14th. Anise is going to pull the work order to see who signed off. Pressure is back to 65 psi now, up from 40. I'd like us to add a valve position check to the closeout checklist so this doesn't happen again, and I'll draft that tonight.

Meeting recap for the writers room. Episode 5 outline is approved with two changes. The cold open moves to the hospital, and the villain's reveal happens in the second act instead of the third. The table read is on the 30th at the main office. Mart is doing a polish pass on Episode 4 this weekend. We also agreed that no episode runs longer than 42 minutes, including credits. The showrunner will send notes on the pilot by Tuesday, and if she's late, we push the read by a day.

Can you help me draft a polite email to a customer who bought tickets for the wrong date? She bought two seats for the Friday show, but she meant the Saturday show, and the Saturday show has only single seats left. Offer her a credit for a future show, or a refund minus the $3 fee, whichever she prefers. Don't blame her, just say it's an easy mistake. Sign it from the box office team, and keep it under 100 words. Oh, and use her name, which is Sophia.

Journal club notes. Dario presented the paper on sparse attention, and the results were actually underwhelming. They only tested on short sequences. The key idea is to attend to a fixed window plus a few global tokens. Wait for the code release before we try to reproduce anything. The offer said it's coming in March. No, the paper doesn't compare against FlashAttention, which is a big gap. We agreed to read the follow up next week. Sorry for the long notes.

Proof handbook update, section on advancement. Scouts earn a badge by completing the requirements and having them signed off by a leader. The review board meets on the second Thursday of each month, because of the church schedule. The board has three members, including one adult who's not a parent of the scout. Scouts should bring their handbook and wear the full uniform. If a scout misses a board, they can reschedule for the following month without penalty. Dario will maintain the sign off log.

Hi Sophia, thanks for the schedule. A couple of requests. I'd like to swap my Thursday afternoon with Sandra's Tuesday morning, if she agrees. I'll also need the second Friday of next month off for a dental procedure. For the new laser machine, the training is two days, not one, and the vendor requires everyone who uses it to be certified. I have a Python function that loads training config, and I want you to review it. The function reads a JSON file, merges it with the command line overrides, and validates the learning rate and batch size. Please check for bugs, especially around the merge order, because last week the default silently overwrote the overrides. My worry about the validation is that it should reject any batch size under 16 and any negative learning rate. Explain the problems in plain English and then show a fixed version, but don't change the function name or the signature, and please keep the type hints.

Hi Babajides, I wanted to explain how the new refund policy works, since a few customers have been confused. If a show is canceled by the theater, everyone gets a full refund automatically within seven days. If the customer cancels, they get a credit instead, as long as they tell us at least 72 hours before the show. Last minute cancellations get nothing, except for medical emergencies, which we handle case by case. Subscribers can transfer their seats to a friend for free, but only up to two times a season. I know it's a lot, so I'll put it on a one page sheet and leave copies at the lobby desk.

And the meeting notes. The new tents will arrive, eight of them, and they're stored in the church basement. Julia is reviewing the insurance policy because it expires on the 31st. The troop will march in the town parade on the 5th of July, since the parade move. We need at least 20 scouts in uniform. Medieval project for Oliver is approved. He'll rebuild the benches at the dog park, about 100 hours of work in total. Next meeting is at the library at 6:30 p.m., and the agenda is the summer camp roster.
